title: Preservation Window SLO policy and graduated circuit-demotion for bursty conversational routes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Bursty conversational routes (chat completions, streaming assistants) cause short-lived large spikes that burn error budgets and trigger blunt failovers. We need a policy that preserves request-quality for active conversations while protecting regional capacity and overall availability.

Goal: Define a Preservation Window SLO construct (time-bounded per-conversation protection), associated SLIs per endpoint/model, and a graduated circuit-demotion and regional-shedding matrix that: 1) prevents noisy short bursts from catastrophically draining error budgets, 2) preserves quality for active sessions, and 3) supports deterministic behavior in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope: engineer-facing SLO/SLI definitions and policy (per-route and per-model variant), automated thresholds for demotion and regional shedding, integration points with routing/traffic arbiter, and operational runbook entries for on-call. Excludes deep changes to runtime kernels or model quantization algorithms (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Define Preservation Window SLO semantics and parameter defaults (window length, eligible sessions, protection budget)
Provide concrete SLI definitions for latency (P50/P95/P99), availability (successful-response-rate), and quality (promptset pass-rate) mapped to each route type
Document error-budget burn-rate rules and automated actions (soft throttle, model demotion, regional shedding) with thresholds and cooldowns
Publish a circuit-breaker escalation matrix with at least three graduated actions and automated rollback triggers
Add integration spec for routing service and console to show Preservation Window state and per-tenant protected sessions
Run a short simulation (synthetic traffic) showing preservation-window prevents >60% of active-session degradations while reducing global error-budget spikes
Provide runbook entries and pager triggers for on-call that reference the new SLO signals
proposal_summary: Introduce a time-bounded 'Preservation Window' concept: when a conversational session issues its first interactive token(s) above a short activity threshold, it is marked as 'preserved' for a configurable duration (default 120s). Preserved sessions get heuristic higher priority for cache/KV-affinity and are protected from immediate model-demotion for a limited preservation budget. When regional capacity stress is detected, the policy first applies graduated demotion to non-preserved sessions, then to buffered preserved sessions, and finally triggers regional shedding only when burn-rate exceeds emergency thresholds.
implementation_plan: Design SLI tags: route:type, session:preserved, model:variant, region - (2 days)
Instrument preservation flag in the routing/service mesh and expose via tracing and metrics (OpenTelemetry) - (3 days)
Add SLO declaration templates for Preservation Windows and default parameters in SLO catalog - (2 days)

Implement circuit-breaker escalation in traffic arbiter with three actions: soft-throttle (delay/queued), model-demote (switch to quantized/cheaper variant), regional-shed (reject non-preserved) - (5 days)
Add automated cooldowns and an error-budget escrow mechanism to allow temporary over-provision for preserved sessions - (3 days)
End-to-end test harness & synthetic burst simulation (replay traffic with preserved markers) - (3 days)
Create Console dashboard tiles and expose Preservation Window metrics per-tenant - (2 days)
Write runbook and run a tabletop exercise with SRE and Solutions - (2 days)
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime-1.20; default off for existing tenants
Stage 1: Internal opt-in for infra tenants and Redwood-owned apps for 2 weeks
Stage 2: Canary enable for 5% of traffic for select high-sensitivity routes (chat/streaming) and monitor SLI deltas
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 50% with monitored burn-rate alerts suppressed to avoid noisy escalation
Stage 4: Full enable and documentation published; enable tenant opt-in in Console
Rollback: instant global disable via feature flag and immediate demotion of preserved markers
metrics_and_sli_definitions: Latency SLI (interactive routes): P95 server-side tail latency per-request (exclude streaming keepalive frames); target: 300ms for low-latency tier
Availability SLI: successful-generation-rate (2xx and valid structured output) per-endpoint; target: 99.8% for tiered routes
Quality SLI: promptset pass-rate measured by canonical unit test suite per-model-variant and per-route; target: 98% for preserved sessions
Preservation Window protected ratio: percent of active sessions marked preserved (instrumentation only metric)
Error-budget burn-rate: 1h and 6h burn-rate windows computed per-endpoint and aggregated per-region
error_budget_policy: Normal: maintain declared SLOs; auto-actions disabled below burn-rate 2x
Caution: burn-rate 2x-5x triggers soft-throttle on non-preserved sessions and increases admission latency (queue for up to 100ms)

Preservation Escrow: each route has a preserved-session escrow (default 10% of regional capacity) that can be consumed to protect active sessions for up to Preservation Window length; escrow replenishes at a configured rate
Emergency: burn-rate >5x across 6h window triggers auto-demote of non-preserved to cheaper variants and enables regional shedding of new sessions
Recovery: define cooldown period (30m) and success criteria (burn-rate <1.2x for 1h) to automatically re-allow preserved protections
circuit_breaker_matrix: Level 1 (warning): per-endpoint burn-rate >2x -> soft-throttle non-preserved; emit pager: no
Level 2 (protect): per-region burn-rate >3x or sustained P95 breaches -> model-demote non-preserved to quantized variant; emit pager: yes (ops-alert)

Level 3 (emergency): cross-region capacity shortfall or burn-rate >5x -> regional shedding enabled for new non-preserved sessions; preserved sessions allowed up to escrow limit; emergency rotation of traffic to fallback region if available
Each level has cooldown hysteresis and a minimum hold time to prevent flappy behavior
private_deployments_notes: Preservation Window semantics must be configurable by operators (window length, escrow size) because on-prem clusters have different capacity profiles
KMS/HSM-sensitive tenants will not have preserved session content routed off-site; preservation markers must be local metadata only
We will provide a light-weight operator CLI to tune thresholds and inspect preserved-session lists in private deployments
Audit logs: preservation state transitions must write to the local audit trail for compliance (private deployments requirement)
